short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status: message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 20870 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

Read that controller's own fault codes; an active source-side fault often explains why the command/status is missing or invalid downstream • 3. If the source controller shows no fault and is transmitting normally, proceed to the link and receiving-controller checks

short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status: message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 20870 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

Typical causes are a connector or wiring fault between the cluster and the backbone, the sending controller going silent, or a faulted cluster module.

step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the cluster fails to display data that is confirmed present on the bus • 2. Remove and replace the gauge cluster per OEM procedure • 3. Program/configure the replacement cluster to the chassis with the OEM tool, clear codes and verify all gauges

short_description: ABS control module message failed checksum validation
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2011 (Loss/invalid data from ABS control module) with FMI 19 (Network-received value flagged as error) is set by the Engine ECU when a value the brake or ABS/ESC system broadcasts on J1939 -- a wheel speed, a brake pressure, a brake/hill-holder switch state, ABS/ASR status, or an external brake request (XBR) -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Engine ECU only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the brake/ABS system's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ABS/ESC controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Engine ECU itself has failed.

fix_title: Confirm the brake/ABS controller is transmitting and check its own active codes
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a J1939 scan tool and confirm the ABS/ESC controller is present on the bus and broadcasting the expected PGN • 2. Read the ABS/ESC controller's own fault codes; an active brake-side fault often explains why the value is missing or invalid downstream • 3. If the ABS/ESC controller shows no fault and is transmitting normally, proceed to the link and receiving-controller checks

short_description: Oxygen sensor heater circuit, bank 2 sensor 1, reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3262 (Oxygen sensor heater circuit, bank 2 sensor 1) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU for the lambda (wideband O2) sensor used to trim the aftertreatment/combustion feedback loop, or for a post-catalyst fuel trim that has moved outside its expected band. A lazy or contaminated sensor and an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor are the most common causes on gasoline- and dual-fuel heavy-duty engines with a three-way or oxidation catalyst.

short_description: SCR downstream NOx sensor internal circuit shorted
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523596 (SCR downstream NOx sensor internal circuit) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for the NOx sensor mounted after the SCR catalyst (measuring tailpipe-out NOx to confirm conversion). fix_title: Replace the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Clear codes, allow the sensor to complete its power-up self-test, and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

short_description: Accelerator pedal position sensor circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 91 (Accelerator pedal position sensor) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the accelerator pedal position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. short_description: ECU EEPROM memory fault
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 630 (Engine control module calibration/configuration fault) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. short_description: EGR valve actuator motor coil circuit open (disconnected)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2971 (EGR valve actuator motor coil circuit) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Engine ECU when the EGR valve actuator will not reach or hold a commanded position, reports an internal fault, loses calibration, or the motor coil circuit is open or shorted.
